description: Data-rights register for the L3VLUP open-data collectors. One entry per external source. 'unverified' means the governing terms were not read or do not answer the question; it is never a guess. Human review is needed for every entry whose businessUse is not 'permitted' and for every field marked unverified.

fields.owner: organisation that owns or issues the data
fields.collectors: scripts in this repo that fetch it
fields.termsReadUrls: pages actually read in this review

sources.source: EDGAR structured data: data.sec.gov submissions, XBRL companyfacts and companyconcept APIs; www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar (filing indexes, index.json, full-index form index, 13F information tables); www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar (SIC lists); efts.sec.gov full-text search; www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json and company_tickers_exchange.json; www.sec.gov/data/foiadocsfailsdatahtm (fails-to-deliver files)
sources.businessUseBasis: sec.gov/privacy.htm: "Information presented on sec.gov is considered public information and may be copied or further distributed by users of the web site without the SEC's permission." SEC-authored material is also a US federal government work (17 U.S.C. 105).
sources.displayRightsBasis: Same clause. Applies to facts and SEC-authored data (holdings tables, XBRL facts, ticker map, fails-to-deliver counts). Third-party authored documents are a separate entry (sec-edgar-filing-documents).
sources.derivedUseRightsBasis: Copying and further distribution are permitted without permission; no restriction on derived works is stated. Facts and calculations from them are not copyrightable.
sources.storageRightsBasis: "may be copied" without permission. The fair-access policy limits request rate, not retention.
sources.redistribution: No restriction on information. SEC seal, logos and EDGAR marks may not be used without a licence. Automated access: max 10 requests/second; the SEC "does not allow 'unclassified' bots or automated tools to crawl the site" and may block IPs. Requests declare an identifying User-Agent (SEC_USER_AGENT) and stay under 10 requests/second; 403/429 stop the letters pipeline outright.
sources.attribution: Requested, not required: "Please consider appropriate citation to the SEC as the source."
sources.notes: Public domain status comes from the SEC's own statement plus 17 U.S.C. 105 for SEC-authored data. 13F holdings are filer-submitted facts, not SEC prose; the privacy page's permission still covers copying and distribution of the page content, and holdings are facts. Cite the SEC as source in the UI where practicable. The request-rate and User-Agent rules are operational conditions to keep access; breach can get the runner IP blocked.

sources.owner: Individual EDGAR filers (authors of the documents); hosted by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.source: Documents filed as exhibits on www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/...: financial advisers' board presentations (Schedule 13E-3 exhibits, EX-99.(C)), activist letters and decks (DFAN14A/13D exhibits), manager letters inside N-CSR shareholder reports
sources.businessUseBasis: The SEC permits copying and further distribution of what is on sec.gov. That grant does not clear the author's own copyright; data/letters.sources.json records the L3VLUP judgement: "The exhibit's author keeps copyright; display is excerpt-only with a link to sec.gov."
sources.displayRightsBasis: Excerpt-only with a credit and a link to sec.gov (data/letters.sources.json rightsNote; data/letters.thumbnail-sources.json rights "sec-public": a preview of the letter page, credited and linked). Full reproduction is not cleared. Manager-website copies are excluded and never fetched.
sources.derivedUseRightsBasis: Measurements, classifications and short claims extracted from the documents are derived facts; verbatim reproduction beyond excerpts is not cleared. Model-extracted claims go to a human review queue before publication.
sources.storageRightsBasis: The pipeline retains no original: documents are fetched into a per-run directory that is deleted at the end (ephemeral-sec mode); only metadata, measurements and WebP previews are committed.
sources.redistribution: Authors keep copyright. Only excerpts and previews with a credit and a link to the filing on sec.gov. No document is cached, proxied or republished whole. SEC fair-access rules apply: 15 MiB cap per document, a 403 or 429 stops the run.
sources.attribution: Credit the filer and link the filing on sec.gov (L3VLUP rule); the SEC asks for citation of the SEC as source.
sources.notes: Not covered by the SEC's public-information statement as to the authors' copyright. Pipeline design already treats these as excerpt-only. A human should confirm that the thumbnail previews (a rendered page of an author's letter) sit inside the excerpt allowance. thesis-pilot.mjs also sends document text to the Anthropic API as a processor; that is a service, not a data source, and its terms are outside this register. sync-market-reference.mjs reads 8-K, 6-K, 10-Q, 10-K and proxy text near a large IEX price move only to classify it (a split ratio, or a spin-off, distribution or reorganisation): the published file carries the classification, a reason of a few words, the form, accession and a link to the document on sec.gov, never the document's text.

sources.source: api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data (CPI, series LNS14000000 unemployment); www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/bls.ics release calendar
sources.businessUseBasis: API terms: "Data accessed through BLS.gov do not, and should not, include controls over its end use." Copyright page: "everything that we publish ... is in the public domain" and "You are free to use our public domain material without specific permission."
sources.displayRightsBasis: Public domain; free use without permission (copyright-information page).
sources.derivedUseRightsBasis: Allowed, but API terms: "Users may not modify or falsely represent content accessed through BLS.gov and still cite the source as BLS.gov." Derived figures (e.g. YoY computed from the index) must not be presented as BLS-published.
sources.storageRightsBasis: Storage is not addressed by the API terms; the data is public domain.
sources.redistribution: No restriction on the data. The BLS emblem/logo may not be used by non-BLS employees. API access may be limited and blocked if limits are exceeded (v1 API: no key, daily query limits).
sources.attribution: Requested: "we do ask that you cite the Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source." Required by API terms: cite the date the data was retrieved, and state that "BLS.gov cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from BLS.gov."
sources.notes: The BLS cannot-vouch disclaimer and the retrieval date are API-term obligations; check that data/macro.auto.json consumers show them wherever BLS-derived series (CPI YoY is computed by L3VLUP) are displayed. Treat this as an open action for the site repo.

sources.source: data-api.ecb.europa.eu SDMX web service (ICP HICP, FM deposit facility rate, YC AAA 10Y yield); www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc (Governing Council dates, HTML); www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-daily.xml (the euro foreign exchange reference rates, one XML file, no key)
sources.businessUseBasis: ECB disclaimer: "users of this website may make free use of the information obtained directly from it"; commercial use is not prohibited (a seller of documents containing it must say it is free on the ECB site).
sources.displayRightsBasis: Free use with the ECB cited as source; information must be reproduced accurately.
sources.derivedUseRightsBasis: Modifications must be disclosed: seasonal adjustment or calculation of growth rates "must be stated explicitly" (statistical data).
sources.storageRightsBasis: Not addressed on the page read. The ECB Data Portal API terms page (data.ecb.europa.eu) returned 503 and was not read.
sources.redistribution: Free use with source cited. Documents bearing authors' names (e.g. Working Papers) cannot be republished in another form without permission. Do not display inside another site's frame for business or promotional linking.
sources.attribution: "the ECB must be cited as the source."
sources.notes: Only the website disclaimer was read. The data portal may have its own terms: unverified. Series are ECB-published except YC, which is an ECB estimate from AAA euro-area bonds. Euro foreign exchange reference rates (added 31 Oct 2026, scripts/fx-rates.mjs, weekly): free to reuse with the ECB cited as source, on the same disclaimer. The ECB's reference-rates page (read 31 Oct 2026) says the rates are published for information purposes only and that using them for transactions is strongly discouraged, so the site uses them for reference figures only (pay bands and career comparisons, rounded to the nearest five thousand) and never for a charge, a product price or a company model. The file re-bases the ECB's quotes to the US dollar (EUR = 1 / USD, GBP = GBP / USD, six decimals), which is a calculation the page states beside the rates: 'Converted ... at the European Central Bank euro reference rates of <date>'.

sources.source: https://iextrading.com/api/1.0/hist (index of daily TOPS/DEEP packet captures) and the Google Cloud Storage links it lists (gzipped pcap, about 15 GB per day, streamed and never stored)
sources.businessUseBasis: IEX Historical Data Terms expressly permit distribution of IEX Historical Data subject to the required attribution. The HIST product is provided free on a T+1 basis. The terms do not state a separate commercial-use restriction for HIST. Sources: Terms of Use clause 01 (distribution or provision of access, with the prescribed attribution); IEX Market Data Policies (September 2026, read in full) s.15: "IEX does not require an IEX Data Subscriber Agreement from any Person who receives, uses, or distributes IEX Historical Data in accordance with the IEX Historical Data Terms of Use."; s.1 defines IEX Historical Data as the T+1 files at iextrading.com/stats/#historical-stats; the fee schedule (effective 1 Oct 2026) charges only for real-time feeds. HIST only: the real-time TOPS and DEEP feeds have their own subscriber agreement and distribution regime, and these rights do not extend to them.
sources.displayRightsBasis: Terms clause 01 expressly contemplates distributing or providing access to IEX historical data, with the prescribed text and link. Clauses 08 and 10: shown as an IEX venue reference point, never as a consolidated market price.
sources.derivedUseRightsBasis: The terms state no separate restriction on calculations from HIST. Conditional on the clause 01 attribution and the clause 08/10 reference-point framing wherever the figures are shown. Clause 03: IEX keeps its proprietary rights in the data. Written confirmation from IEX is optional, for the record.
sources.storageRightsBasis: The terms state no separate storage restriction for HIST. Conditional on keeping it private: the collector keeps the daily database only in the Actions cache, never committed or published; only the daily reference file and weekly shards are published. Written confirmation from IEX is optional, for the record.
sources.redistribution: Clause 01: any distribution or access requires the attribution below. Clause 03: IEX keeps ownership of the data. Clauses 08 and 10: the data covers IEX trading only and is "a reference point only, rather than ... a basis for making trading decisions". Clauses 04-07, 09: as-is, no warranty, indemnity by the user.
sources.attribution: Data provided for free by IEX. By accessing or using IEX Historical Data, you agree to the IEX Historical Data Terms of Use. (with a link to https://www.iex.io/legal/hist-data-terms)
sources.notes: Approved 19 Oct 2026 as the default $0 market-reference source for Finance OS. Scope: HIST (T+1) only, never the real-time TOPS or DEEP feeds. Published as a dated "IEX reference price" with the disclaimer "Venue-specific IEX reference price; not a consolidated closing price." Open action: optional written confirmation from IEX Market Data (draft in docs/market-reference.md s.1).

sources.owner: The publishers already registered for the newsflow and deal-tape feeds, and L3VLUP (its own sitemap)
sources.source: The pages linked from items already collected into data/newsflow.auto.json and data/deals.auto.json (at most ten a week, one request a second, 15 s timeout), and https://www.l3vlup.com/sitemap.xml
sources.termsUrl: unverified: each page is governed by its publisher's terms, registered under that publisher's feed entry; hosts whose feed entry reads businessUse restricted (Bloomberg) are never fetched and the editor sees the headline only
sources.businessUseBasis: Inherits each publisher's entry. The pages are read once, in the run, so that one bounded model call can draft an edition for a human editor; the editor reads every figure at the source before anything is published.
sources.displayRightsBasis: Nothing from a page is displayed. The published file carries each source's URL, publisher name, date and headline (already in the feeds) and the draft text the model wrote; the 3,200 characters of page text read in the run are held in memory and never written to the file.
sources.derivedUseRightsBasis: The draft edition is a summary written for an editor's review, with every figure to be checked at its source before publication.
sources.storageRightsBasis: No page text is stored. The feed items themselves follow their own entries' retention.
sources.redistribution: unverified
sources.attribution: The draft names each source's publisher and links the page; the published edition cites its sources by URL.
sources.notes: Reads only what the registered feeds already link. A restricted host is skipped by code (restrictedHosts in lib/this-week-draft.mjs). The site's own sitemap is L3VLUP's own property.
